SOVEREIGNTY AND SELF-DETERMINATION

By Bekele Shume

A short life and a narrow scope

Sovereignty is not something natural but a notion brought about by human beings. According to the most widely held conception, sovereignty describes a state that stands with a defined and known people and territory and that possesses the full competence to decide, both in its internal administration and in its external relations, without any commanding or coercive power over it. Let us leave aside for the moment whether the notion is concretely realized: for countries to have this kind of character, they must first recognize and respect one another’s existence. Before this historical stage, human beings had travelled an extremely long evolutionary road. The way of life that carves the earth into “my country” and “your country” is a product of time. There was indeed an era when human life was not far removed from the herd life of wild animals that cooperate in obtaining food and in defending themselves from attack. Out of this natural foundation of mutual aid there came, through long evolution, complex social relations and the improvement of life through knowledge and craft.

Using tools to bring down fruit, to hunt and to fish; turning from using crude tools as they are to improving them; moving from eating food raw to cooking it; overflowing with food and satiety when fortune favoured and staggering with hunger when it did not — in the struggle to escape that alternating existence, on the one hand learning the technique of preserving surplus food by salting and drying it in the sun, and on the other tying one’s existence to places where better food and water and milder climates were to be found; grasping how crops germinate and bear fruit and so passing from gathering to seed-cultivation; passing from hunting animals to penning, keeping and domesticating them; through such knowledge winning the victory of being able to own a permanent surplus (property); through that decisive victory, deaths caused by food shortage declining and human numbers multiplying into clans and tribes; the multiplication of people in turn driving the expansion of farming and animal husbandry; broad families led by elders and founding villages tied to farmland appearing here and there; broad families growing into clans, and related clans devising further bonds and ties; beyond shifting cultivation, the discovery of manuring the land and obtaining a greater surplus by that method; the permanent ownership of surplus in turn multiplying the free time in which people could exercise their minds on improving crafts and ways of living; along with the multiplication of occupations and of clans, the creation of higher forms of organization and division of labour (leader and led, commander and commanded, the one who enforces custom and security and punishes its breach, the one who guards and expands the holding against rivals and leads fighters, and the like) — it is evolutionary changes of this kind, linked one to another, that produced the phenomena called “country” and “state.”

Alongside the appearance of “country” and “state” — that is, of human collectives whose existence revolves, settled or mobile, within a given area and which have devised a certain order of organization — living securely within one’s holding, in mutual respect and without attacking one another, did not come along with it. Just as there were places where the chance of knowing what lay in distant regions was blocked by natural limits (mountain chains, the barrier of seas and oceans, unconquered for want of the means of civilization), so that peoples lived without touching one another — indeed, just as peoples have been found meeting the present age without having moved beyond ancient hunting, fishing and rudimentary farming and herding, and without wearing clothes — so migration under the pressure of natural disasters, harsh climatic changes and social causes, striking and pushing others aside, and then campaigning again against those who had been pushed, has been the long, unending history of humankind. The discovery, in stages, of copper, bronze and iron brought a leap forward in agriculture, in handicraft and in the art of war, and produced societies unequal in civilization and in fighting capacity; and beyond seizing booty in scattered raids there appeared a warrior-hood that made its wealth by invading and plundering. On that side, instead of killing and driving out the defeated, the taking of captives to be worked as slaves and to be sold arose; and instead of deporting them, the making of them subjects (tribute-payers) where they stood. The way the ancient civilizations built up their multi-territorial character (empire) derives from just such a process.

When the Roman Empire, the most famous and mighty of all empires, extended beyond Europe into Asia and Africa, and when the Aksumites campaigned to the north-west and to the east (crossing the sea) and later turned southward, there was no such thing as violating sovereignty. If one had power, to spread and to expand was in those days a praiseworthy deed. When the core and the western part of the Roman Empire collapsed and broke apart, the eastern part somehow organized itself, made Constantinople (today’s Istanbul) its capital, took Greek instead of Latin as its working language, adopted Christianity and carried on. The Islamic expansionism that campaigned in every direction from the seventh century onward, wrested territory from the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire and reached as far as ruling parts of Europe, likewise knew nothing of countries living side by side in mutual respect. The loose western “Holy Roman” Empire, which arrived with the ninth century and spread out with its centre around Germany, could have no connection with the idea of sovereignty: it saw itself as the extension of God’s absolute authority and counted campaigning, or having others campaign, against those outside Catholicism — whom it called “heretical Christians” or “non-Christians” — as a holy act. Neither the Habsburg line, which sprang up essentially in Austria and, intertwined with the “Holy Roman Empire,” spread its royal stock into a widely interlocked rule within Europe, nor the other absolutist regimes, were free of the warlike expansionist style. The Ottoman Turkish Empire, which rose at the beginning of the 14th century, expanded and swallowed southern Europe (in the second half of the 14th century) and later the Byzantine Empire (in the 15th century), and stretched its palm as far as northern and eastern Africa, was likewise a subjugator. The history of colonization that spread over the world from the 16th century of exploration and “discovery,” when Spain was ascendant, until the end of the 19th century, when Britain and France emerged on top, contradicts the idea of sovereignty and is in large measure a product of warrior-hood.

Even at the level of Europe, the spreader of colonial rule, it is hard to say that living together in mutual recognition and respect as free (independent) countries had properly taken hold by this time. Britain herself was created by a history of English subjugation that began inside Europe. Following the French Revolution of 1789, the empire-building wars of two Napoleons replaced republican administrations. The Austrian Habsburg Empire, whose territorial extent fluctuated, lasted into the 20th century (the First World War). The Ottoman Turkish Empire too struggled on until the First World War without releasing a certain part of Europe. Bosnia, which had escaped the weakened Turkish palm before the war, did not escape being swallowed by Austria-Hungary. Even the First and Second World Wars were wars in which there appeared not only the desire to re-divide the colonial holdings among the old grabbers, but also the desire to tear territories out of Europe itself and emerge huge and mighty.

The stage in which the empires within Europe and the Turkish Empire crumbled and many free countries were created may be said to hold a special place in the history of sovereignty. The idea of self-determination too came along with this process. The League of Nations and the United Nations (UN) are also forums in which countries have made the effort to live together with formal recognition of equality and through diplomacy. Even so, effort and actual accomplishment, the idea of sovereignty and its practical realization, must not be confused. Rather than blaming the League of Nations for failing to defend its member Ethiopia from the Italian invasion, it would express the truth better to say that it handed her over as a sweetener to appease Italy. Since, for the continents of Africa and Asia (including certain parts of Latin America) that were more or less direct colonial subjects, the era of the League of Nations and the UN was an era in which, until they won “independence,” they did not even see the custom of raising a flag and calling themselves a country, to describe that era as the era of sovereignty would be partisan — unless the world is taken to mean Europe and its extra limbs (North America and Australia).

It is no wonder that formerly a king whose power was unlimited was called absolute (sovereign). Under the Ethiopian Constitution issued in 1923 E.C., “the land of Ethiopia, and its people, and its law, in their entirety, belonged to the Emperor.” But it is astonishing that some, in order to connect the era of imperialist might and of direct colonial empires with “sovereignty,” have coined the phrase “imperial sovereignty.” Would it not be laughable if we said that when Britain attacked Italy inside her East African colonial holding she was violating Italy’s “imperial sovereignty”?

Most of the Latin American countries that became more or less free in the 19th century, as well as the countries that, following the first half of the 1950s, emerged from direct colonialism, raised flags and won UN membership, did not, beyond formal sovereignty, attain to being the supreme deciders of their own internal and external affairs in the way the conventional idea of sovereignty implies. Bound in semi-colonial, dependent economies, indirectly steered within the superpower bloc struggle led by America and the Soviet Union, many of them were arenas of contention convulsed by the many-sided struggle in which one superpower sought to uproot the other’s puppet and plant its own. Broadly speaking, “sovereignty,” together with the creation of international associations of organization (the League of Nations, the UN), served to keep member states away from war (to reconcile them), but it did not do away with intervention and invasion. In world history the desire to change countries’ borders is a problem that has existed to this day (one that pops in and out along with military superiority and a neighbour’s weakness). When Somalia invaded Ethiopia in 1969 E.C. she had taken note of Ethiopia’s political crisis. When Iraq’s Saddam invaded Kuwait on a pretext in the summer of 1982 E.C., he was emboldened by his superiority in force. America and the others came to Kuwait’s aid not out of anxiety for her sovereignty but because their oil-related interest outweighed it and because they were superior in force. Today, in the 21st century, when Russia sliced Crimea off Ukraine, the reason Europe, America and NATO did not attempt to take it back by force was also that Russia’s military capacity was not something they could easily dispose of (the outcome might not have been Russia’s loss alone). In short, from the creation of the world association of states until today, the chief assurance and means of self-protection for preserving one’s existence unattacked has been being strong and not being outweighed in the balance of power.

Alas, alas for “sovereignty”!

When the Soviet Union broke apart and the contest of the two blocs was interrupted, and when on America’s side the reason for propping up clients for the sake of superpower position was lost, what followed was the staggering of the dependants of both sides, as though their crutch had vanished; disintegration and fragmentation as well as unification — changes of the map — and the strengthening of the voice of democracy and justice. Those for whom neither continuing under the old regime nor achieving a new change worked out were fated to writhe in prolonged chaos. As obtaining the Western assistance led by America came to require entering into democratic administration, the new (bloc-free) international situation was, broadly, one that relatively permitted the freedom to strive without being a superpower’s retinue, and was favourable to the spread of democracy. Along with the democracy movement, better than at any earlier time, the demand to take each country’s “sovereign” decisiveness out of the palm of dictators and monarchs and place it in the hands of the people (popular sovereignty) came to be heard strongly in the pre-industrial countries.

Even so, the result was determined by the seasoning of many things and did not escape being contradictory. Although a reality freed from being locked into blocs made reliance on one’s own effort imperative, being able to develop by one’s own separate effort was, and still is, just as hard a test. Just as new democratic constructions appeared, dictators were also able to use the fashion of the day, “democracy,” as a mask to hide behind. In not a few countries even that failed, and being trampled under merciless despotism, or a mutual annihilation of a kind that makes one wish for colonial subjugation again, reached such a pitch and found no end that it made intervention proper and just. In connection with these contradictory tendencies, the separate “sovereignty” of countries and the “decisiveness” of self-determination grew old and were laid to rest without having established an identifying epoch in the world and without being properly married to the decisiveness of peoples. From the orderless conflict of Somalia that erupted in the 1980s, through Burundi, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Liberia, the land of the former Yugoslavia, and the massacre- and displacement-producing conflicts that have come since and are still coming, the lameness of sovereignty stands exposed.

They have shown plainly that when despots, sheltering behind non-interference in internal affairs, carry out fascist massacres and “cleanse” ethnic groups, or when a state aborts and a country is devoured, standing by in silence is not respecting sovereignty but sharing in the atrocity; that intervening to stop it and supporting the restoration of law and order is a responsibility both of civilization and of being human; that the socio-political crisis that befalls one country is not confined to that country but, through its crisis-spreading danger — terror, the varied ills of sea and land, and the trouble of displacement — becomes a problem of the neighbours and of the rest of the world as well; and that even if the political order and capacity by which one country’s oppressive rulers and war profiteers might be held to account by their own people is lacking, they ought to be held to account before the world community. In that spirit, intervening for better or worse to stop crises and bringing oppressors to justice began some time ago. Yet intervention of this kind has not escaped losing its direction and being used as a plaything of superpower interest. America’s interventions, alone or together with her partners (in Panama, Yugoslavia, Sudan, Libya, Iraq, Afghanistan, Syria and so on), are cases in point.

Through the gap opened by America and NATO, the small ones too have entered. The crisis of the Democratic Republic of Congo came to be endless because of the interference and meddling of neighbours driven by narrow interest. In the turmoil of the Horn of Africa, much has been said about the gun and the intrigue of new and small Eritrea. The interventionist efforts and negotiations to rid Somalia of the banditry of the warlords failed one after another, and the country even came to be a hatchery of religious extremism and of sea piracy, not only because of the warlords’ greed but because she was a field of proxy rivalry for her neighbours as well, and because within the joint effort to establish a government that would impose law and order there were squabbles over planting a loyal client. Today, bringing down the rod upon a state that one calls a threat to one’s security has become unsurprising. In this same spirit Ethiopia has delivered “proportionate” punishment against the Eritrean government after the war.

The “sovereign right” of a government to request assistance has also been seen to become a commodity and a mockery for military intervention. The Saudi Arabian-led invasion, which had no use whatever except to devastate Yemen rather than lift her out of crisis, was launched holding a “permission” which said that a non-existent government (a leader who had fled into Saudi Arabia) had requested help. Just as Syria’s Bashar al-Assad talks about Syria’s sovereignty and about his own sovereign statehood, so too in Iraq, which has become a threshing-floor of terror and of military interventions, the aborted government was heard shouting, in Tahsas 2008 E.C., “Turkey has brought her soldiers in without my permission, she has violated my sovereignty…” It would have been more apt had it objected that Turkey’s main desire was, hidden under cover of fighting the “Islamic” terrorism created by caliphal rule, to attack the Kurds who were the main force of that war. But its shouting as though it had a sovereign life showed how far sovereignty has come to be a thing devoid of meaning. From this angle, it would not be undue boldness to say, as some political analysts have said, that sovereignty is a word that ought to be erased from the dictionary. On the other hand, just as treating a country’s internal administration, under the customary idea of sovereignty, as the business of the state alone, into which no one may slip, has to some degree restrained one country from swelling against another, so it has also served as a shelter behind which rulers commit atrocities against their own people unchecked.

Although the continuous imposition by peoples of their interest upon the leadership of government through representative democracy is a thing not yet grasped anywhere in the world (including within the great democracies), two hundred years have passed since the history began, with the Great French Revolution (1789), in which the appointment and removal of rulers came into the palm of the people’s vote. Although since the French Revolution there have been differences of speed and movement forward and backward, choosing among parties and having rulers appointed by the people for a limited term has long been so customary among the developed Western countries as to seem to have been created along with them. In the countries called the “Third World,” however, making genuine popular decisiveness systematic and lasting keeps slipping away and causing difficulty. Drafting a fine constitution and then, after coming to power through election, twisting the administration by various devices and building an election-clad dictatorship; gathering applauders into parliament and dressing up the desires of despotism as the people’s decision; blessing massacres as having been carried out for the safety of the people and of the country — such shamelessness has become customary. The ruler of Burundi who extended his term of office in 2008 E.C. also offered, as the reason for his interest in power, that he was necessary for the country’s development and for the continuation of democracy. The growing opposition of peoples both to stretching the constitution so as to lift term limits and to military coups indicates that the desirability of democracy is widening. Even so, making parliament a gathering place of genuine representatives of the people and a genuine organ of popular decisiveness is a work that has barely begun and that involves a many-faced struggle bound up with the economy, with culture and with human development.

Whether or not state power is connected with the people’s power to appoint and to call to account, in our world the fate of countries is, from time to time, more and more interdependent and interlinked rather than self-determined. That the fate of one is determined by others, and that of others by one, has become glaring. Let us take something that seems not to reach others, something that seems to concern only oneself. If a country decided that it wished to live self-sufficiently, touching others in nothing, that would be like going mad or hanging oneself. Here one may meet disputants who say that the meaning of sovereignty lies not in whether the decision is sound, but in the right to make a decision that may count as sound or as deranged. Deciding — who over whom? If a leader gave such a decision, he would be passing judgment on the rights of the people. If the people’s representatives were the deciders, they too would be touching the rights of the whole people. If the whole people decided by majority vote, it would not escape passing judgment on the existence of those outvoted. Even for those willing to do so, making a decision equivalent to saying “let us destroy our lives” is not a right. Beyond that, their decision would not remain confined to themselves but would enter into the fate of their children and of the coming generations. And so even a decision saying “I will touch no one” becomes a matter counted as a violation of human rights and fit for intervention. If we note, as this simple example shows, that in every kind of exercise of “self-determination” there is an entering into the rights of another, it is easy to see that an epidemic disease or a pest arising in one country becomes the internal affair of other countries even before it crosses the border, and that the abortion of government that occurs in one country and the civil war, terror and mass displacement that follow are, more than for anywhere else, the internal affair of the neighbouring countries.

That the interdependence stands out most sharply among neighbours holds for small and great alike. America’s history is closely bound up with the countries around her. In the history of the Latin American countries we find North America as a helper toward independence, and in conflict as well as in economic intercourse. “New Mexico,” which lies inside America, is a relic of the history of war. The internal affairs of both America and Mexico are deeply entangled with the countries’ mutual (foreign) relations. America cannot plan the control of drug trafficking inside her country without citing and including her foreign relations. A change in American law concerning migrants concerns American employers and the hopefuls of migration from Latin America through to Africa and Asia. The embargo America has imposed on Cuba, now fifty years old, may look on the surface like a punishment, but it shows how much neighbourliness entails the interlocking of each other’s existence. Just as Cuba’s history of emerging from direct colonialism was convenient for Americans to take good lands and become insiders, so the expropriation brought by the Cuban revolution crushed not only Cubans but American property owners as well. And for the American government and its magnates, Cuba’s “socialism” was a headache like living in one compound, startled awake, with a system-enemy called the Soviet Union. And so the weaving of endless espionage, assassination and subversion plots, from the days of the bush struggle onward, was all a wrestling to save oneself from being eaten — and so was the embargo. Today’s (2008 E.C.) resumption of relations, just as it is a hope for the Cubans who were left behind, is for America the conducting of a decrepit enemy’s funeral and the use of a capital and commodity market at her door.

The terror attack in the city of Paris in Hidar 2008 E.C. (at a football ground, a restaurant and a concert hall), which took 130 lives and wounded some 370 people, was cross-border in its organization; and the work of uprooting the attackers’ chain could not be completed within the map of one country and required the joint effort of Europe — a good illustration of how the boundary between internal and external affairs is becoming mixed. It is the same with Ethiopia and her neighbours. Her neighbours’ economic, population-related, political and religious affairs cite Ethiopia. And Ethiopia’s many-sided movement cites each of them. Just as her neighbours have a contribution in determining Ethiopia’s fate, Ethiopia too has a share in determining theirs. We may describe this relationship by saying that her neighbours’ map has a long tip that touches her border, and that Ethiopia’s map likewise goes beyond Sudan and enters into Egypt.

But our focus upon close neighbours should not make us forget that the interdependence can go far beyond neighbours. We are seeing migration and terrorist activity arising in the “Third World” for various reasons crossing over into the great countries, and the anger of terror that the great countries themselves stoked sucking up the wretched countries as well. The air-polluting way of life of China and India, of America or of other countries, has not remained a debt that is the internal affair of those countries. Through its recurrent and lasting consequences there have followed others’ loss of health and of a morsel, the scramble over denuded areas and the disruption of their struggle against poverty, and for some the fate of being covered over and lost beneath ocean water. And since the overall safety of our earth is demanding a commitment to bring the increase of heat and of pollution at least down to zero, the agreement reached in France this year to keep the earth’s temperature rise below two degrees centigrade itself, apart from trimming a little of the wrong being done today and tomorrow by pollution, has sanctioned the continuation of that wrong. Pollution, in its capacity as a natural destroyer, entering into countries’ internal affairs, narrowing poor countries’ room for manoeuvre and unsettling them, and damaging the fortune of the coming generation, has not ceased. But in the end, a time is bound to come when not only the release and burial of polluting matter, and not only the destruction of forest, but even the failure to develop forest will be a matter for which countries are held to account and punished.

In short, the attainment of reliable world security, growth and peace requires, for many, a greater struggle against air pollution than today’s and than the customary; a change in the general style of living aimed at the chief polluters; the spreading of development by sharing with weak countries the craft and knowledge that is the comfort of a few countries, rather than tossing alms and accepting refugees; and, more than trying to spy out, hunt down and destroy terrorists, the singling out and opposing of the superpower partiality, interventionism and meddling that is, in general, the chief hatcher and breeder of terror. (Leaving aside terror’s other background and related causes: as a report presented by the BBC in 2008 E.C., supported by insider information, exposed, the “Islamic” terror state established in Iraq was fundamentally a product of the invasion carried out against Saddam’s Iraq — conceived within the invader’s prison camps, which were not poor in injustice, and later grown by feeding upon aggrieved Sunnis and upon Saddam’s scattered soldiery. To wrestle with the acts of terror that arise in each country without opposing such parenting and fostering of terror by the mighty is labour without end.) And all this struggle in turn requires coming out of striving separately and helping one another and rallying together by creating many-sector links in various forms.

The continental and sub-continental groupings seen in each continent are a reflection of this. Even so, their depth and breadth vary according to each grouping’s focus. The matter of controlling local security, terror, illicit trades, the conflicts of border communities and the like depends upon coordinating the capacity for it and working together. The desire to create a common trade zone requires understanding and agreement on exchange policy, on the free movement of goods, on a common tariff, on taxation and on such matters. Creating an economic community that goes as far as the use of a common currency requires going deeper still — following and harmonizing the soundness of things that could directly or indirectly shake the value of the common currency (members’ economic growth, the stability of their politics, their tax-collection competence, the interplay of their imports and exports, their debt burden and their borrowing practices, their unemployment rates and so on).

In Africa too, from the African Union, which holds the vision of making Africa one united continental country, to unions and communities of various regional horizons, groupings have been created and are still being created. (The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA), the inter-governmental coordination created by the countries of the Horn of Africa, IGAD, the East African Community (still at the design stage), the Community of Sahel-Saharan States and the like may be mentioned.)

The lasting development of African countries also seems to require, beyond the present kinds of grouping, a political linkage that dries up conflicts and brings better stability and respect for human beings. The areas of West Africa, East Africa and Central Africa, where social intermixing unbounded by the man-made border is intense, are good examples of this. The peace and stability of the areas of Rwanda, Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda probably requires, by way of reconciliation and democracy, the creation of at least a confederal union. The separation of South Sudan, too, was not something demanded by the age of consolidation and by the development we are in, but was brought about by a regime that failed to understand the times and to turn to just treatment and mutual benefit. Even now, South Sudan’s stability and growth requires being arranged within the East African or the Horn of Africa linkage rather than struggling on alone.

From what has been said so far the following conclusions may be set down:

- The straightening out of countries’ fortunes has come to hang more and more upon leaning on one another and upon collective mutual aid rather than upon striving separately. Indeed, the sub-continental and continental tendency to group together that is seen today suggests that the time when the number on the world map declines and the slogan “long live my country” grows old will not be very far off.

- Every country, through the agreements and obligations it has entered into by virtue of its membership in an international organization or in a continental or sub-continental grouping, has things that are subtracted from the individual country and transferred to the grouping, that come back as limits upon members, and that member countries respect and are held to account for, whether as norms or as decisions. That is why isolating a country by institutional decision and pressing it with sanctions is seen to be practised.

- The era in which criminal rulers confuse matters in the name of sovereignty and escape accountability has also ended.

- In a country where the administration of government has aborted and chaos prevails, many “internal affairs” are exposed to becoming entangled with foreign intervention.

a4705.t:
- More than 200 planeloads of aid have been flown to parts of Syria since the devastating earthquake struck.
- Nearly half of the aid is from the UAE.
- The quake killed more than 3 600 people in Syria.
More than 200 planeloads of aid have been flown to government-held parts of Syria since the February 6 earthquake, nearly half from the United Arab Emirates, an official said Wednesday.
The aid has come mostly from allies of President Bashar al-Assad's government since the 7.8-magnitude quake struck the war-torn country and neighbouring Turkey, killing more than 45 000 people.
"Until now 213 planes carrying quake aid have landed in Syria", including 92 from the UAE, Suleiman Khalil, an official from Syria's transport ministry, told AFP.
After more than a decade of war, Assad's government remains a pariah in the West.
But the earthquake that killed more 3 600 people in Syria has sparked Arab outreach to his internationally isolated government, which was expelled from the Arab League after the conflict erupted in 2011.
The UAE, the first Gulf country to normalise ties with the Assad government after a years-long boycott, is largely spearheading regional relief efforts.
Its health minister Abdul Rahman al-Owais went on an official trip Tuesday to Syria's quake-hit coast, which is under government control, and told reporters he wished for "a united stance globally to face this huge humanitarian challenge".
ALSO READ | SA rescue workers safe after second Turkey earthquake, says Islamic Relief
The latest flight to land in Damascus was a Norwegian plane carrying 14 tons of Red Cross aid including large tents with stoves, water pumps and water purification equipment.
"Those affected are very vulnerable due to years of war and crisis," said Joergen Haldorsen of the Norwegian Red Cross.
Damascus also made an official plea to the European Union for help two days after the deadly earthquake struck, with the EU commission encouraging members to respond to the request.
Syria's civil war, which was triggered by the government's suppression of pro-democracy demonstrations, has claimed around 500,000 lives and displaced around half the country's pre-war population.
Even before the earthquake, most of the population was in need of humanitarian assistance. The latest disaster has only piled on more misery.

a4763.t:
Ex-Associate Justice Kabineh M. Ja’nah says he is mobilizing lawyers to challenge the legality of the 2025 National Budget in court.
By Lincoln G. Peters
Monrovia, Liberia, December 24, 2024 – Former Associate Justice Kabineh M. Ja’nah vows here to sue the Government of Liberia, particularly the Executive Branch of Government, if President Joseph N. Boakai signed the controversial Fiscal Year 2025 budget.
Speaking on Spoon Midnight conversation, Cllr. Ja’nah said that he has spoken to a few senior lawyers, and they are planning that the moment President Boakai signs the Budget, which they believe was passed illegally, they will take the matter to the Supreme Court.
“If the President signed this Budget into law that we believe was not legal at all and didn’t meet the requirements, we will take the government to the Supreme Court to ask for a Legal Declaratory of Properties as to the way this budget was passed. Now, we are not doing this to say oh, this is what we’re going to do to the Supreme Court; we will bring it to the court and say: please make a declaration whether the passage of this budget met the legal requirements under our system”, he explains.
According to him, the way they want to do it is by starting from the lower court and after that, they will go to the Supreme Court based on the decision from the lower court, adding that they want the court to clearly state the procedure.
The Liberian Senate over the weekend unanimously concurred with the Majority bloc of the House of Representatives on the passage of the Fiscal Year 2025 National Budget in the amount of US$880.07 million.
Members of the Liberian Senate took the decision late Friday, December 20, 2024, following a motion from Grand Kru County Senator Numene Bartekwa. However, of the 30 senators, 19 voted in favor of the budget.
Prior to the senate passage of the Budget, the majority bloc passed the budget at the Monrovia City Hall (MCC) in a special emergency session.
Meanwhile, following the passage of the 2025 National Budget and subsequent concurrent by the Liberian Senate, embattled House Speaker J. Fonati Koffa labels the Majority Bloc’s recent passage of the 2025 national budget as ultra vires.
“Ultra vires”, Cllr. Koffa posted on his official Facebook page on December 21, 2024.
Ultra vires is a Latin phrase that means “beyond the powers” or “lack of power.” It’s a common law principle that describes when a person or entity acts without legal authority. The doctrine of ultra vires is most relevant in corporate law, administrative law, and constitutional law. It ensures that laws are made legally and that corporations and government agencies act within their powers. Editing by Jonathan Browne

a4865.t:
Somali finance minister fired after suspending corrupt officials associated with the president
                 |
                  09 July 2023 18:36 
            
            
		
 
        
			MOGADISHU (HORN OBSERVER) – Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre has dismissed Finance Minister Dr. Elmi Mohamud Nur just two days after the minister suspended two officials linked to President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud over allegations of corruption and abuse of power.                        
	
		
            
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
		
    The announcement was made by Farhan Jimale, the spokesman of the Office of the Prime Minister, during a mini reshuffle on Saturday night, appointing Bihi Iman Egeh as the new finance minister.
The replacement came after a consultation with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, the spokesman added.
The sudden sacking of Minister Nur has left many Somalis in shock, especially as it came a day after he was compelled to retract his official statement suspending Accountant General Mohamed Abdirahman Anas and the Finance Ministry’s Director for Revenue, Feisal Mohamed Hashi.
In his initial letter, Minister Nur accused the two officials of various misconduct, including actions detrimental to national interests, obstruction of the ministry’s administration, deliberate payment delays, unwarranted salary withholding, and hindrance to accessing the Somalia Financial Management Information System (SFMIS), a World Bank and IMF-supported financial reporting system.
‘Stern warning’
However, in an unexpected turn of events, Minister Nur reversed his decision on Friday, stating that the suspensions were lifted but emphasizing that the administrative charges remained, serving as a stern warning for future conduct.
Official sources have revealed that President Mohamud exerted pressure on Minister Nur to rescind the suspensions, as the two officials involved are closely associated with the president.
Both Mohamed Abdirahman Anas (pictured left) and Feisal Mohamed Hashi (right) have longstanding connections to President Mohamud’s political party. Anas, in particular, has been a longtime friend and party member, having come from SIMAD University, which was co-owned by President Mohamud before he joined the Premier Bank, another institution affiliated with the president. Hashi, the Director of Revenue, also hails from SIMAD University and has been an active member of President Mohamud’s political party.
The sacked officials are regarded as highly influential figures in the government’s financial sector, with one insider stating that they hold significant responsibility for releasing funds, including kickbacks for the president and his family.
Don’t touch those connected to the big fish
The abrupt dismissal of these powerful individuals, who are connected to influential figures within the government, has raised concerns about the extent of corruption within Somalia’s political landscape.
Political analyst Ahmed Ali has criticized the sacking, suggesting that Minister Nur should not have dared to dismiss these influential individuals due to their close ties to powerful figures within the government, including President Mohamud.
"For your own survival, you don’t touch those connected to the big fish,” he said.
Meanwhile, MP Ayub Ismail of the Somali Federal Parliament has described the situation as a serious matter that affects the entire government, emphasizing the limited power of both the prime minister and the finance minister to fulfill their constitutional duties.
"Where the head of government does not have any power to fulfill his constitutional duties, one can imagine how limited the power of the minister is. Therefore, this move is not surprising,” MP Ismail, who also comes from the region as minister Nur, said.
In response to his removal from office, Minister Nur expressed his accomplishments during his tenure, highlighting that he ensured timely payment of government employees’ salaries and attempted to maintain a non-political approach to financial reforms.
"I tried to keep politics out of the financial reform program. I have tried to maintain the institutional system of the Ministry of Finance so that it can efficiently fulfill its mandate, so that we can effectively serve our people,” he wrote on his Facebook.
However, the events surrounding his dismissal have further exposed the widespread corruption within the Somali government. Many citizens have begun to point fingers at President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, accusing him of granting economic benefits to his family members, relatives, and friends while nearly half the country’s population still need humanitarian assistance, including 230,000 at serious risk of starvation.

a4926.t:
Selon un communiqué du Cabinet Royal, Sa Majesté  Mohammed VI , Roi du Maroc, le 24 octobre 2025, au Palais Royal de Rabat, des entretiens avec le Président de la République française, S.E.M. Emmanuel MACRON, qui effectue une Visite d'État au Maroc, du 28 au 30 octobre, à l'invitation du Souverain.
Les entretiens entre les deux Chefs d’Etat ont porté sur le passage vers une nouvelle ère des relations fortes entre le Maroc et la France, dans le cadre d'un Partenariat d'exception renouvelé et d'une feuille de route stratégique pour les années à venir ;
Selon le communiqué du Cabinet Royal, le Président de la République française a adressé une invitation officielle à Sa Majesté  Mohammed VI , Roi du Maroc pour effectuer une visite d'Etat en France. Invitation que le Souverain a acceptée, et dont la date sera convenue par le canal diplomatique".
Dans le cadre de cette même visite d’Etat, Sa Majesté  Mohammed VI , Roi du Maroc, et SE Monsieur Emmanuel MACRON, ont signé, lundi 28 octobre 2024, au Cabinet Royal à Rabat, la Déclaration relative au "Partenariat d’exception renforcé" entre le Royaume du Maroc et la République française, en vue de permettre aux deux pays de mieux répondre à l’ensemble des défis auxquels tous deux sont confrontés, en mobilisant tous les secteurs pertinents de la coopération bilatérale, régionale et internationale.
S’agissant du Sahara marocain, la Déclaration relative au "Partenariat d’exception renforcé" entre le Royaume du Maroc et la République française, souligne que «  Les deux Chefs d’Etat ont souligné que le "Partenariat d’exception renforcé" entre le Maroc et la France avait vocation à être mis en œuvre dans le champ d’application territorial le plus large possible, à la lumière de la position française exprimée à l’occasion du 25ème anniversaire de l’accession au Trône de Sa Majesté, dans laquelle le Président de la République a souligné : "je considère que le présent et l’avenir du Sahara occidental s’inscrivent dans le cadre de la souveraineté marocaine. […] Pour la France, l’autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine est le cadre dans lequel cette question doit être résolue. Notre soutien au plan d’autonomie proposé par le Maroc en 2007 est clair et constant. Pour la France, celui-ci constitue désormais la seule base pour aboutir à une solution politique juste, durable et négociée conformément aux résolutions du Conseil de sécurité des Nations Unies ».
Également, lors de cette visite d’Etat, Le Souverain, que Dieu L'assiste et le Président MACRON, ont présidé, la soirée de ce lundi 28 octobre 2024, au Palais des Hôtes Royaux à Rabat, la cérémonie de signature de plusieurs accords entre le Royaume du Maroc et la République française.
Ci-après :  le texte intégral du communiqué du cabinet Royale :
"Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L’assiste, a eu, ce jour, au Palais Royal de Rabat, des entretiens avec le Président de la République française, S.E.M. Emmanuel Macron, qui effectue une Visite d'État au Maroc, du 28 au 30 octobre, à l'invitation du Souverain.
Les entretiens entre les deux Chefs d’Etat ont porté sur le passage vers une nouvelle ère des relations fortes entre le Maroc et la France, dans le cadre d'un Partenariat d'exception renouvelé et d'une feuille de route stratégique pour les années à venir.
A cet égard, les deux Chefs d'Etat entendent, à travers ce partenariat renouvelé, donner une impulsion décisive aux relations multidimensionnelles d'excellence entre le Maroc et la France, pour tenir compte des ambitions des deux pays et faire face, ensemble, aux évolutions et défis internationaux.
Les entretiens ont, également, porté sur les questions régionales et internationales. Ainsi, les deux Chefs d'État sont convenus d'œuvrer de concert pour conforter la projection euro-méditerranéenne, africaine et atlantique, dans une démarche d'action commune en faveur de la prospérité et du développement humain et durable.
Ils ont souligné l'importance de renouveler, en profondeur, le partenariat entre les deux rives de la Méditerranée, pour construire un avenir plus stable, durable et prospère pour l'ensemble de la région, tout en répondant aux enjeux socioéconomiques et environnementaux actuels.
Par ailleurs, le Président de la République française a salué le rôle constructif de Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L’assiste, Président du Comité Al-Qods, au service de la paix au Moyen-Orient. Les deux Chefs d'Etat ont appelé à une cessation immédiate des attaques à Gaza et au Liban, tout en soulignant la priorité de protéger les populations civiles, et l'importance de garantir et fluidifier l'acheminement d'une aide humanitaire suffisante, tout en mettant un terme à l'embrasement régional. Le Souverain et le Président français ont rappelé l'urgence de réactiver le processus de paix, dans le cadre de la solution à deux États, avec un État Palestinien indépendant, sur les frontières du 4 juin 1967, avec Jérusalem Est comme Capitale.
Le Président de la République française a adressé une invitation officielle à Sa Majesté Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L’assiste, pour effectuer une visite d'Etat en France. Invitation que le Souverain a acceptée, et dont la date sera convenue par le canal diplomatique".

State Visit of President MACRON to the Kingdom of Morocco

According to a communiqué from the Royal Cabinet, His Majesty Mohammed VI, King of Morocco, held talks on 24 October 2025 at the Royal Palace in Rabat with the President of the French Republic, H.E. Mr Emmanuel MACRON, who is making a State Visit to Morocco from 28 to 30 October at the invitation of the Sovereign.

The talks between the two Heads of State focused on the transition towards a new era of strong relations between Morocco and France, within the framework of a renewed Exceptional Partnership and a strategic roadmap for the years to come;

According to the communiqué from the Royal Cabinet, the President of the French Republic extended an official invitation to His Majesty Mohammed VI, King of Morocco, to make a State Visit to France. The Sovereign accepted the invitation, the date of which will be agreed through diplomatic channels.”

In the framework of this same State Visit, His Majesty Mohammed VI, King of Morocco, and H.E. Mr Emmanuel MACRON signed, on Monday 28 October 2024, at the Royal Cabinet in Rabat, the Declaration on the “Reinforced Exceptional Partnership” between the Kingdom of Morocco and the French Republic, with a view to enabling the two countries to better respond to all the challenges both face, by mobilising all relevant sectors of bilateral, regional and international cooperation.

With regard to the Moroccan Sahara, the Declaration on the “Reinforced Exceptional Partnership” between the Kingdom of Morocco and the French Republic underlines that “The two Heads of State stressed that the ‘Reinforced Exceptional Partnership’ between Morocco and France was intended to be implemented within the broadest possible territorial scope, in the light of the French position expressed on the occasion of the 25th anniversary of His Majesty's accession to the Throne, in which the President of the Republic stated: ‘I consider that the present and the future of Western Sahara fall within the framework of Moroccan sovereignty. […] For France, autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty is the framework within which this question must be resolved. Our support for the autonomy plan proposed by Morocco in 2007 is clear and constant. For France, it now constitutes the only basis for reaching a just, lasting and negotiated political solution in accordance with the resolutions of the United Nations Security Council.'”

Also, during this State Visit, the Sovereign, may God assist Him, and President MACRON presided, on the evening of Monday 28 October 2024, at the Palace of Royal Guests in Rabat, over the ceremony for the signing of several agreements between the Kingdom of Morocco and the French Republic.

Below is the full text of the communiqué from the Royal Cabinet:

“His Majesty King Mohammed VI, may God assist Him, held talks today, at the Royal Palace in Rabat, with the President of the French Republic, H.E. Mr Emmanuel Macron, who is making a State Visit to Morocco from 28 to 30 October, at the invitation of the Sovereign.

The talks between the two Heads of State focused on the transition towards a new era of strong relations between Morocco and France, within the framework of a renewed Exceptional Partnership and a strategic roadmap for the years to come.

In this regard, the two Heads of State intend, through this renewed partnership, to give decisive impetus to the multidimensional relations of excellence between Morocco and France, in order to take account of the ambitions of the two countries and to face, together, international developments and challenges.

The talks also covered regional and international issues. Thus, the two Heads of State agreed to work together to strengthen the Euro-Mediterranean, African and Atlantic projection, in a joint approach in favour of prosperity and human and sustainable development.

They underlined the importance of profoundly renewing the partnership between the two shores of the Mediterranean, in order to build a more stable, sustainable and prosperous future for the whole region, while responding to current socio-economic and environmental issues.

Furthermore, the President of the French Republic hailed the constructive role of His Majesty King Mohammed VI, may God assist Him, Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, in the service of peace in the Middle East. The two Heads of State called for an immediate cessation of the attacks in Gaza and Lebanon, while stressing the priority of protecting civilian populations, and the importance of guaranteeing and facilitating the delivery of sufficient humanitarian aid, while putting an end to the regional conflagration. The Sovereign and the French President recalled the urgency of reactivating the peace process, within the framework of the two-State solution, with an independent Palestinian State, on the borders of 4 June 1967, with East Jerusalem as its Capital.

The President of the French Republic extended an official invitation to His Majesty King Mohammed VI, may God assist Him, to make a State Visit to France. The Sovereign accepted the invitation, the date of which will be agreed through diplomatic channels.”

Vor 50 Jahren 7. Mai 1975
30 Jahre nach Kriegsende
Berlin (Ost) - Seit Beginn dieses Jahres laufen die Vorbereitungen in der DDR für eine Großfeier des Tages ,,der Befreiung", die 30. Wiederkehr des 8. Mai 1945, als die deutsche Wehrmacht des Dritten Reiches bedingungslos kapitulierte. Während im Westen nicht annähernd so viel Aufhebens von dem Jahrestag gemacht wird, lancieren die Ostblockstaaten, allen voran die DDR, eine beispiellose Kampagne, worin die Rolle der Sowjetarmee als die große Befreierin verherrlicht wird. Fast jede Ortschaft der DDR feierte am entsprechenden Tage den Einzug der Befreier. Die staatliche Presse der DDR wiederholt in großen Aufschriften immer wieder die Botschaft, daß der deutsche Faschismus aus dem imperialistischen Stadiun des Kapitalismus entstanden sei. Der Krieg wird als eine bittere Auseinandersetzung zwischen reaktionärer imperialistischer Herrschaft und dem erneuerten Sozialismus, verkörpert in der Sowjetunion, dargestellt. Die offizielle kommunistische Geschichtsdarstellung bezeichnet die Schlachten, die an der deutsch-sowjetischen Front ausgetragen wurden, als die entscheidenden. Der Endsieg habe eine zutiefst menschliche Gesellschaftsordnung über ein barbarisch imperialistisches System errichtet.
Die Reden, Pressekommentare und ausführlichen Analysen in ideologischen Zeitschriften betonen wiederholt den Verlust sowjetischen Lebens (20 Millionen). Die Verluste des Gegners und der Alliierten werden dabei übergangen. Die DDR betrachtet sich als völlig neuen deutschen Staat, der insgesamt mit der imperialistischen Vergangenheit abgerechnet hat.
Zu den Feiern am 8. Mai sind zahlreiche russische Kriegsveteranen des Zweiten Weltkrieges geladen. Darunter sind auch einige, die die sowjetische Flagge auf dem Reichstagsgebäude pflanzten. Große Plakate stellen allerorts den sowjetischen Soldaten als den Befreier, Freund und Kameraden dar.
Lynchjustiz in Kambodscha
Washington - Nach einer Meldung des amerikanischen Außenministeriums nehmen die Khmer-Rouge-Truppen die Hinrichtung hoher politischer und militärischer Gefangener in Kambodscha vor. Das Außenministerium entnimmt diese Annahme einer Radiosendung aus Kambodscha. Mindestens 80 Führer mit ihren Frauen wurden in einem ländlichen Bezirk hingerichtet. Der Außenminister Henry Kissinger sagte in einem Fernsehinterview, daß es bekannt sei, daß in Kambodscha tragische und unmenschliche Dinge geschehen. Inzwischen dauert die großangelegte Evakuierung der Südvietnamesen von der pazifischen Insel Guam und von den Philippinen an. Bis zu 150 000 Vietnamesen und kambechanische Flüchtlinge werden in den USA erwartet.
Transfusion mit „Eigenblut"
München/Dortmund - Bis zu 37 Prozent der Patienten in aller Welt erkranken nach Fremdblut-Übertragungen an infektiöser Gelbsucht. Jeder zehnte Transfusionskranke stirbt. Wesentlich weniger Risiken birgt ein Verfahren in sich, das jetzt am Max-Planck-Institut für Systemphysiologie in Dortmund und am Institut für chirurgische Forschung der chirurgischen Universitätsklinik in München erprobt wird. Kranke erhalten eigenes Blut, das ihnen vor der Operation abgenommen wurde, nach dem Eingriff wieder zurück.
Bei diesem Verfahren, das inzwischen auch Kliniken in den USA und in Mannheim anwenden, wird der Verlust an Eigenblut vor dem Eingriff zunächst durch eine Ersatzflüssigkeit ausgeglichen. Der Patient kann also während der Operation nur ,,gestrecktes" Blut verlieren. Das fehlende Volumen gleicht er dann nach dem Eingriff mit seinem eigenen frischen, ,,Vollblut" aus.
Nach Angaben der Max-Planck-Gesellschaft zeigte sich bei Tierversuchen mit Hunden, daß auch die Entnahme größerer Blutmengen keine nachteiligen Folgen hat. Selbst wenn der Anteil der roten Blutkörperchen bei den Versuchshunden auf ein Viertel sank, bestand keine Lebensgefahr.
Beim Menschen, so fanden die Wissenschaftler, ist die Blutentnahme von ein bis maximal zwei Litern im Normalfall ungefährlich. Allerdings kann dieses Verfahren nur bei geplanten Operationen und einem vorher abschätzbaren Blutbedarf angewendet werden. Für Notfälle bleiben Blutkonserven mit all ihren Nachteilen weiterhin lebenswichtig.
Attentat auf General Franco?
Madrid - Ein geparktes Auto explodierte außerhalb des Madrider Fußballstadions am Donnerstagabend, kurz nach der Ankunft von Staatsoberhaupt General Franco zur Vereinigten Handelsausstellung. Der gestohlene Wagen, der laienhaft mit einem kleinen explosiven Gegenstand ausgestattet war, explodierte eine halbe Stunde nach Eintreffen des 82-jährigen Generals. Der General befand sich in Begleitung des Prinzen Juan Carlos von Bourbon und Regierungsabgeordneten. Im Dezember 1973 fiel Premierminister Luis Carrero Blanco einem Attentat zum Opfer, als unter seinem Auto eine Bombe explodierte, das sich auf der Fahrt durch Madrid befand. Aus Polizeiberichten geht hervor, daß General Franco auf keinen Fall verletzt worden wäre, auch wenn das geparkte Auto etwa 100 m vom Haupteingang des Bernabeu-Stadions explodiert wäre, während der General den Haupteingang passierte. General Franco selbst berührte dieser Zwischenfall in keiner Weise, und einige Minuten später sprach er lachend zu einer 60 000-köpfigen Menschenmenge, die ununterbrochen, Franco, Franco" rief. Personen wurden bei dem Zwischenfall nicht betroffen.

50 Years Ago, 7 May 1975

30 Years After the End of the War

East Berlin – Since the beginning of this year, preparations have been under way in the GDR for a grand celebration of the day "of liberation", the 30th anniversary of 8 May 1945, when the German Wehrmacht of the Third Reich surrendered unconditionally. While in the West nowhere near as much fuss is being made of the anniversary, the Eastern Bloc states, above all the GDR, are launching an unprecedented campaign glorifying the role of the Soviet Army as the great liberator. Almost every locality in the GDR celebrated the arrival of the liberators on the corresponding day. The GDR's state press repeats again and again, in large headlines, the message that German fascism arose out of the imperialist stage of capitalism. The war is portrayed as a bitter confrontation between reactionary imperialist rule and renewed socialism, embodied in the Soviet Union. The official communist account of history describes the battles fought on the German-Soviet front as the decisive ones. The final victory, it holds, established a profoundly humane social order over a barbaric imperialist system.

The speeches, press commentaries and detailed analyses in ideological journals repeatedly emphasise the loss of Soviet lives (20 million). The losses of the enemy and of the Allies are passed over. The GDR regards itself as an entirely new German state that has settled accounts with the imperialist past in its entirety.

Numerous Russian veterans of the Second World War have been invited to the celebrations on 8 May. Among them are some who planted the Soviet flag on the Reichstag building. Large posters everywhere depict the Soviet soldier as liberator, friend and comrade.

Lynch Justice in Cambodia

Washington – According to a report by the American State Department, Khmer Rouge troops are carrying out the execution of senior political and military prisoners in Cambodia. The State Department draws this conclusion from a radio broadcast from Cambodia. At least 80 leaders, together with their wives, were executed in a rural district. Secretary of State Henry Kissinger said in a television interview that it is known that tragic and inhuman things are happening in Cambodia. Meanwhile the large-scale evacuation of South Vietnamese from the Pacific island of Guam and from the Philippines continues. Up to 150,000 Vietnamese and Cambodian refugees are expected in the USA.

Transfusion with One's Own Blood

Munich/Dortmund – Up to 37 percent of patients worldwide fall ill with infectious jaundice after transfusions of donor blood. One in ten transfusion patients dies. Considerably fewer risks are carried by a procedure now being tested at the Max Planck Institute for Systems Physiology in Dortmund and at the Institute for Surgical Research of the surgical university clinic in Munich. Patients receive back, after the operation, their own blood that was taken from them beforehand.

In this method, which clinics in the USA and in Mannheim now also use, the loss of the patient's own blood before the operation is first compensated for with a replacement fluid. The patient can therefore lose only "diluted" blood during the operation. He then makes up the missing volume after the procedure with his own fresh "whole blood".

According to the Max Planck Society, animal experiments with dogs showed that even the removal of larger quantities of blood has no adverse consequences. Even when the proportion of red blood cells in the test dogs fell to a quarter, there was no danger to life.

In humans, the scientists found, the withdrawal of one to at most two litres of blood is normally harmless. However, this procedure can only be used for planned operations and where the blood requirement can be estimated in advance. For emergencies, stored blood with all its disadvantages remains vitally important.

Assassination Attempt on General Franco?

Madrid – A parked car exploded outside the Madrid football stadium on Thursday evening, shortly after the arrival of head of state General Franco at the United Trade Exhibition. The stolen vehicle, amateurishly fitted with a small explosive device, blew up half an hour after the arrival of the 82-year-old general. The general was accompanied by Prince Juan Carlos of Bourbon and government deputies. In December 1973 Prime Minister Luis Carrero Blanco fell victim to an assassination when a bomb exploded under his car as it was being driven through Madrid. Police reports indicate that General Franco would on no account have been injured, even if the parked car had exploded about 100 m from the main entrance of the Bernabeu stadium while the general was passing through the main entrance. General Franco himself was not affected in any way by the incident, and a few minutes later he spoke laughingly to a crowd of 60,000 people who chanted "Franco, Franco" without pause. No persons were harmed in the incident.

a5230.t:
Grangemouth, Scotland’s only oil refinery, is to close in 2025 with the loss of 400 jobs, operator Petroineos said, according to a report by Reuters.
Daily Trust reports that this is coming amidst the rollout of premium motor spirit (PMS) from the Dangote refinery, which significantly reduced importation of PMS.
Reuters quoted Petroineos as saying it was preparing to shut Grangemouth, Britain’s oldest refinery as production ceases in the second quarter of next year, subject to an employee consultation, a company spokesperson said.
The decision was however criticised by trade unions and politicians.
- Kidnappers gun down Hotel owner, manager, guest despite N25m ransom
- Mob sets 2 ‘bandits’’ corpses ablaze in Kaduna
“It is deeply disappointing that Petroineos have confirmed their previous decision to close Grangemouth oil refinery,” UK Energy Secretary Ed Miliband said.
Reuters further reports that the site will become an import and distribution terminal for finished fuels, which will cut the number of employees at the site from 475 to around 75 over the next two years.
Petroineos is a joint venture between PetroChina International London (PCIL) and INEOS Group, a British chemicals firm founded by billionaire Sir Jim Ratcliffe.
The company cited economic difficulties as the reason for the closure, stating that the company had invested $1.2 billion since 2011, and returned losses in excess of $775 million over the same period.
“Grangemouth is increasingly unable to compete with bigger, more modern and efficient sites in the Middle East, Asia and Africa. Due to its size and configuration, Grangemouth incurs high levels of capital expenditure each year just to maintain its licence to operate,” the company said.
It said the plant is currently losing around $500,000 per day, and expects to see a $200 million loss for 2024.
Analysts have said the commencement of operation by the Dangote refinery would significantly reduce fuel importation, thereby affecting the businesses of many refineries outside Africa.
The refinery operation is a business that thrives on volume and analysts anticipate closure of more refineries in Europe if more African countries invest in domestic refining.
The federal government of Nigeria is also working on reviving its refineries in Port Harcourt, Kaduna and Warri.

a5253.t:
Mogadishu, (SONNA) — The Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA), Mohamud Macalin Abdulle, today held an important meeting with Ahmed Aden Hameed, Head of the Qatar Red Crescent Office in Somalia.
The discussions focused on strengthening cooperation between the two institutions, particularly in disaster preparedness and response, humanitarian assistance, and building the capacity and skills of SoDMA staff to effectively manage emergency situations.
The Head of the Qatar Red Crescent commended SoDMA for its consistent efforts in addressing humanitarian challenges, reaffirming the organization’s commitment to continue supporting development initiatives and providing urgent assistance to vulnerable communities.
For his part, the SoDMA Commissioner highlighted the importance of sustained collaboration, stressing that the partnership between the two agencies will help deliver durable and practical solutions to reduce the vulnerability of Somali communities.
SoDMA reiterated its commitment to expanding cooperation with both international and local partners in order to enhance the safety, resilience, and well-being of the Somali people.

a5264.t:
The USAID’s Youth Empowerment Activity has surpassed its halfway target after graduating 14,000 young people with literacy and business skills across 14 counties in South Sudan in the first two of the four-year initiative.
The latest round of YEA graduation held at Juba Technical Secondary School on Thursday, has passed out 490 youth including 254 females and 236 males.
Implemented by Education Development Center (EDC), the program launched in August 2022 has now surpassed the halfway mark of the targeted 25,000 beneficiaries of the four-year project.
Addressing the event, U.S. Ambassador to South Sudan, Michael J. Adler emphasizes the importance of investing in education as a foundational pillar for a country’s development.
Amb. Adler encouraged the South Sudan government to allocate public revenue transparently and appropriately across all its sectors.
“We know this is just a fraction of the millions who need access to these opportunities. Transitional government investment in education is not optional,” he said.
“It is essential to building a peaceful, prosperous, and self-reliant generation that can help build a better future for this country. So I renew our call in the transitional government to start using public revenue transparently and appropriately to support public education as well as other basic services.”
He suggested adequate school funding and timely payment of teachers and lecturers to foster a stable and prosperous future for South Sudanese youth.
“Teachers must be paid on time and schools must receive the funding they need to operate. The United States remains committed to helping the people of South Sudan. This commitment is decades old.”
“It predates the independence of this country. It began and remains based on values, belief in peace, human rights, democracy, and a government responsive to its people’s needs.”
Amb. Adler further said the YEA reflects a longstanding commitment from the United States to support the people of South Sudan, rooted in shared values of peace, human rights, democracy, and accountability in governance.
He stated that the transitional government’s underinvestment in education, has prevented millions of youth from accessing essential educational opportunities.
He called on government officials to take education responsibility and not depend solely on donor support.
“For too long, there has been underinvestment by the transitional government in public education. Millions of South Sudanese youth lack access to the education and opportunities they need to realize their full potential.”
“Representatives of the ministries, this cannot be left to donors alone to address. The youth empowerment activity is helping by providing foundational literacy and numeracy skills, entrepreneurial training, and knowledge about critical topics.”

a5271.t:
Kujenga nidhamu ya mtoto huenda sambamba na umri alionao kwa wakati huo, na vyote viwili hutegemea hatua ya ukuaji wa ubongo aliyopo mtoto husika ambapo hatua ya ukuaji wa ubongo humsaidia mtoto kukabiliana na hisia zake.
Ubongo wa mtoto mwenye umri kati ya miaka miwili hadi sita hukua kwa kasi sana, ambapo hisia zao huwa juu, lakini uwezo wa kudhibiti hisia hizo bado huwa haujakomaa.
Watoto wa umri huu wanaweza kuonyesha tabia kama kurusha vitu wakiwa na hasira, kukataa kufuata maagizo, au kulia kwa nguvu wanapokosa wanachotaka. Ingawa wazazi wengi huchukulia tabia hizi kama ukosefu wa nidhamu, ukweli ni kwamba hali hizi ni za kawaida na zinaweza kudhibitiwa kwa msaada wetu sisi wazazi.
Kwa nini watoto hukosea? Ni kwa sababu sehemu ya mbele ya ubongo wa mtoto, ambayo kwa kitaalamu inatiwa prefrontal cortex, inayohusika na fikra na udhibiti wa hisia, bado haijakomaa.
Hii ina maana kwamba watoto wanategemea zaidi hisia zao badala ya kufikiria matokeo ya hisia hizo. Kwa sababu hiyo, wanakosea mara kwa mara bila kuelewa athari za tabia zao.
Dk Daniel Siegel, profesa wa saikolojia na mwandishi wa kitabu cha The Whole-Brain Child, anasisitiza kwamba watoto wanapokosea wanahitaji kuongozwa na sio kuadhibiwa au kuaibishwa. Hapa ndipo dhana ya nidhamu chanya inapoingia, kwa kuwafundisha watoto kudhibiti hisia na tabia zao kwa njia zinazowajenga badala ya kuwaumiza.
SOMA ZAIDI: Watoto wa Miaka Mitano Wana Harakati Nyingi. Mbinu Hizi Zitakusaidia Kukabiliana Vizuri
Katika tamaduni nyingi, adhabu za kimwili kama viboko na zile za kihisia kama vile kufoka bado zinachukuliwa kuwa njia sahihi ya kuwaadabisha watoto. Ingawa zinaweza kuleta matokeo ya haraka, tafiti zinaonyesha kwamba viboko na kufoka mara nyingi husababisha hofu na nidhamu ya woga badala ya kuelewa.
Adhabu hizi zinaweza kuathiri vibaya afya ya akili na kujiamini kwa mtoto, zinaongeza tabia ya fujo na kupunguza uwezo wa kujidhibiti na zinadhoofisha uhusiano kati ya mzazi na mtoto.
Pia, adhabu hizi zinaweza kumuumiza mtoto, kusababisha majeraha na hata kifo kama tulivyosikia taarifa ya hivi karibuni ya mtoto Chloy aliyepoteza maisha baada ya kuchapwa na mwalimu wake.
Kwa mfano, Chama cha Madaktari wa Watoto cha Marekani (AAP) kimebaini kuwa adhabu za kimwili zinaweza kujenga tabia ya ukatili kwa watoto wanapokuwa watu wazima, kwani hujifunza kutumia vurugu na ubabe kutatua migogoro na changamoto.
Nidhamu ya hofu haijengi nidhamu ya kweli bali nidhamu ya woga na tabia za udanganyifu.
Ili kuwasaidia watoto kukuza nidhamu ya kweli, tunapaswa kutambua hisia za mtoto. Watoto mara nyingi hukosea kwa sababu hisia zao zimewaelemea. Tunapowatambua na kuthibitisha hisia zao, tunawasaidia kuelewa makosa yao na jinsi ya kuyarekebisha.
SOMA ZAIDI: Kwa Nini Watoto Wadogo Wanapenda Kurusha Vitu?
Kwa mfano, tunapomwambia mtoto aliyekasirika, “Ninaelewa umechukia, lakini kumpiga mwenzako sio sahihi. Njoo uniambie ukiwa na hasira badala ya kumpiga mwenzako,” tunamfundisha njia bora ya kudhibiti hasira yake.
Watoto pia hujifunza vizuri wanapojua wazi kinachotarajiwa kutoka kwao. Wazazi wanapaswa kuwaelekeza watoto kuhusu sheria za nyumbani kwa upendo na kuwakumbusha mara kwa mara.
Mifano ya mipaka dhahiri inaweza kuwa, “Tunasafisha meza baada ya kula” au “Hatusemi maneno ya ya matusi.”
Au, badala ya kuwaadhibu, tunaweza kuwasaidia watoto kujifunza kutatua changamoto zao. Kwa mfano, tunapomuuliza mtoto kwa upendo, “Kwa nini unalia?” au “Nini kimekukasirisha?” tunawasaidia kutambua sababu za hisia zao. Hii huwafundisha kufikiria kabla ya kutenda na kuwapa ujuzi wa kutatua migogoro.
Watoto pia hujifunza zaidi kwa kuiga tabia za watu wazima wanaowazunguka. Tukiwaonesha nidhamu, heshima, na jinsi ya kushughulikia changamoto kwa utulivu, nao pia watajifunza tabia hizo. Hii inajumuisha jinsi tunavyoongea, tunavyofanya kazi, na tunavyoshughulikia hisia zetu.
Tunapochagua mbinu mbadala za adhabu, tunaimarisha uhusiano wa heshima na uaminifu kati yetu na watoto. Hili linawafanya watoto kuwa tayari zaidi kushirikiana na kujifunza kutoka kwetu.
SOMA ZAIDI: Fanya Haya Kumsaidia Mtoto Kuanza Kujisaidia Mwenyewe kwa Kutumia Poti au Choo
Mbinu hizi husaidia watoto kudhibiti tabia zao, na pia kujenga ustadi muhimu wa maisha kama kudhibiti hisia, kutatua changamoto, na kuonyesha huruma kwa wengine. Tunapowasaidia watoto kuelewa makosa yao badala ya kuwaadhibu, tunawajengea msingi imara wa maadili, heshima, na uwajibikaji.
Kwa kuwekeza katika nidhamu chanya, tunawaandaa watoto wetu kwa maisha yenye mafanikio na mahusiano mazuri.
Badala ya kuogopa mamlaka, wanajifunza kuiheshimu. Badala ya kutenda kwa hasira, wanajifunza kutenda kwa busara. Hatimaye, tunachangia kuunda kizazi chenye nidhamu ya kweli na uwezo wa kuishi kwa maelewano na wengine.
Makala hizi za malezi huandaliwa na C-Sema, shirika lisilo la kiserikali linalojikita katika kuendeleza na kulinda haki za watoto Tanzania. Kwa maoni na ushauri, wapigie kwenye simu namba 116, ambayo ni maalumu kwa huduma za mtoto. Huduma hii haitozi malipo toka mitandao yote nchini. Vilevile, unaweza kuwapata kupitia kurasa za Facebook: Sema Tanzania, X: @SemaTanzania, na kupitia tovuti yao www.sematanzania.org.
a5271.en:
Building a child's discipline goes hand in hand with the age they are at that time, and both depend on the stage of brain development the child in question is at, where the stage of brain development helps the child to deal with their emotions.

The brain of a child aged between two and six years grows very fast, and their emotions run high, but the ability to control those emotions is still not mature.

Children of this age may display behaviour such as throwing things when angry, refusing to follow instructions, or crying loudly when they do not get what they want. Although many parents regard these behaviours as a lack of discipline, the truth is that these situations are normal and can be managed with help from us parents.

Why do children make mistakes? It is because the front part of the child's brain, which is technically called the prefrontal cortex, which is responsible for thinking and control of emotions, is still not mature.

This means that children rely more on their emotions rather than thinking about the consequences of those emotions. For that reason, they make mistakes repeatedly without understanding the effects of their behaviour.

Dr Daniel Siegel, a professor of psychology and author of the book The Whole-Brain Child, stresses that when children make mistakes they need to be guided and not punished or shamed. This is where the concept of positive discipline comes in, by teaching children to control their emotions and behaviour in ways that build them up rather than hurt them.

READ MORE: Five-Year-Old Children Are Very Active. These Techniques Will Help You Cope Well

In many cultures, physical punishments such as caning and emotional ones such as shouting are still considered the right way to discipline children. Although they may bring quick results, studies show that caning and shouting often cause fear and a discipline of fear rather than of understanding.

These punishments can badly affect a child's mental health and self-confidence, they increase aggressive behaviour and reduce the capacity for self-control, and they weaken the relationship between parent and child.

Also, these punishments can injure a child, cause wounds and even death, as we heard in the recent report of the child Chloy who lost her life after being beaten by her teacher.

For example, the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) has found that physical punishment can build a habit of cruelty in children when they become adults, because they learn to use violence and domination to resolve conflicts and challenges.

Discipline based on fear does not build true discipline but rather a discipline of fear and habits of deception.

To help children develop true discipline, we should recognise the child's emotions. Children often make mistakes because their emotions have overwhelmed them. When we recognise and validate their emotions, we help them understand their mistakes and how to correct them.

READ MORE: Why Do Small Children Like Throwing Things?

For example, when we tell an angry child, "I understand you are upset, but hitting your friend is not right. Come and tell me when you are angry instead of hitting your friend," we teach them a better way to control their anger.

Children also learn well when they know clearly what is expected of them. Parents should guide children about the rules of the house with love and remind them regularly.

Examples of clear boundaries can be, "We clean the table after eating" or "We do not use insulting words."

Or, instead of punishing them, we can help children learn to solve their own challenges. For example, when we ask a child lovingly, "Why are you crying?" or "What has made you angry?" we help them identify the reasons for their emotions. This teaches them to think before acting and gives them skills for resolving conflicts.

Children also learn more by imitating the behaviour of the adults around them. If we show them discipline, respect, and how to handle challenges calmly, they too will learn those behaviours. This includes how we speak, how we work, and how we handle our own emotions.

When we choose alternative methods to punishment, we strengthen the relationship of respect and trust between us and the children. This makes children more ready to cooperate and to learn from us.

READ MORE: Do This to Help a Child Start Using the Potty or Toilet on Their Own

These techniques help children control their behaviour, and also build important life skills such as managing emotions, solving problems, and showing compassion to others. When we help children understand their mistakes rather than punishing them, we build for them a firm foundation of values, respect and responsibility.

By investing in positive discipline, we prepare our children for a successful life and good relationships.

Instead of fearing authority, they learn to respect it. Instead of acting out of anger, they learn to act with wisdom. Ultimately, we contribute to creating a generation with true discipline and the ability to live in harmony with others.

These parenting articles are prepared by C-Sema, a non-governmental organisation focused on promoting and protecting children's rights in Tanzania. For comments and advice, call them on telephone number 116, which is dedicated to child services. This service is free from all networks in the country. You can also reach them through their Facebook page: Sema Tanzania, X: @SemaTanzania, and through their website www.sematanzania.org.

a5348.t:
Les décisions des Américains de suspendre le financement de la réponse nationale éthiopienne au VIH auront des conséquences particulièrement graves, touchant plus de 270 000 bénéficiaires dans les régions d’Oromia, de Gambella et à Addis-Abeba, selon un avertissement du Programme commun des Nations Unies sur le VIH/SIDA (ONUSIDA).
Les récentes décisions des Etats-Unis de suspendre le financement de la réponse nationale éthiopienne au VIH seront « particulièrement graves », affectant plus de 270 000 bénéficiaires dans les régions d’Oromia et de Gambella, ainsi qu’à Addis-Abeba, a averti le Programme commun des Nations Unies sur le VIH/SIDA (ONUSIDA).
